name: DONUT
notes: DONUT is structurally a fixed-target beam-dump experiment, but its defining physics purpose -- direct detection of tau-neutrino interactions from an accelerator-produced neutrino beam -- matches the accelerator-neutrino category used for KARMEN, LSND and OPERA, so it is classed as an accelerator-neutrino experiment with fixed-target as a secondary kind.
No official DONUT/Fermilab website was reachable (fnal.gov returned HTTP 403 to every access attempt, as also noted on facility:fermilab), so no website is recorded rather than a guessed one.
No INSPIRE experiment lookup was performed for DONUT, so external.inspire_experiment is left empty (the INSPIRE literature record that was opened did not render usable content).

The detector placement site is site:fermilab-main-campus, an existing record already used for several other Fermilab short-baseline experiments' near detectors; it is referenced here rather than duplicated, because two sites of one facility within 100 m would be redundant.

physics_goals.value: Directly detect interactions of the tau neutrino, the last lepton of the Standard Model not yet directly observed

summary.plain: A Fermilab experiment that ran for a few months in 1997, aiming a proton beam from the Tevatron at a target to make tau neutrinos and catching them directly for the first time in stacks of photographic emulsion, completing the direct detection of every particle the Standard Model predicts.
summary.technical: Fermilab fixed-target experiment (E872) using a Tevatron proton beam dump to produce tau neutrinos from charmed-meson decay, detected via nuclear-emulsion targets combined with electronic scintillator/drift-chamber tracking. Ran in 1997; its 2001 analysis of 203 neutrino interactions found four tau-neutrino candidate events (background 0.34 events), the first direct observation of tau-neutrino interactions.
